title: Chicken Caesar wraps
skill: Whisking a dressing and tasting it

notes.text: Toss the salad in two bowls, with half the dressing in each, so it coats evenly.

move.title: Whisk, taste, fix, roll
move.body: This is the unit's mastery week: you make it on your own. You'll whisk a creamy Caesar dressing, taste it and fix it, toss it with romaine, rotisserie chicken, and parmesan, and roll it all up in big tortillas.

why.title: No raw eggs here
why.body: Old-style Caesar dressing uses raw egg yolks, which can carry germs. Store mayonnaise is made with pasteurized eggs, gently heated to kill germs, so this dressing is creamy and safe without cooking.

why.title: Whisk until smooth
why.body: Lemon juice and mayonnaise don't blend on their own at first. Whisking in quick circles spreads the lemon all through, so every bite tastes the same.

why.title: Taste, then fix one thing
why.body: A dressing is right when it tastes right to you. Taste it on a lettuce leaf. Too sharp, add a little mayonnaise. Flat, add a pinch of salt or a squeeze of lemon. Change one thing, then taste again.

why.title: Dry leaves hold the dressing
why.body: Dressing slides off wet lettuce, and the water left on the leaves makes it thin. Lettuce patted dry lets the dressing cling, and keeps the wrap from going soggy.

why.title: Fold the sides, then roll
why.body: Folding in the sides first closes the ends of the wrap. Rolled up tight from the bottom, it holds together without a toothpick.

wrong.fix: Whisk in water, 1 teaspoon at a time, until it drips slowly off the whisk.

wrong.sign: The tortilla cracks when you roll it
wrong.fix: Warm it for 10 seconds in the microwave under a damp paper towel so it bends.
Use less filling, fold the sides in first, and roll tightly. Set it seam side down.
Dry the lettuce well, and toss and roll right before eating.

quiz.q: Where do you taste the dressing?
What do you do before rolling the wrap?
choices: Fold the sides over the filling

substitutions.note: Gluten-free tortillas crack when cold. Warm each one for 10 seconds before you roll it.
Greek yogurt makes a tangier dressing. Taste it before adding all the lemon juice.

steps.text: Read the recipe through. Set out every tool and ingredient before you start.
steps.tip: This is your mastery week. You make it on your own.

steps.text: Wash your hands. Pull the chicken meat off the bones with two forks or clean fingers.
steps.look: About 2 cups of meat, no bones or skin.

steps.text: Tear the chicken into bite-size shreds and put it on the plate. Put the bones in the trash.
steps.tip: Put the rest of the chicken back in the fridge now.
Chicken grease on your fingers makes everything slippery.

steps.text: In the small bowl, whisk the mayonnaise, lemon juice, garlic, mustard, Worcestershire if you're using it, the dressing's parmesan, and the pepper.
steps.look: Smooth and creamy, with no streaks of lemon.

steps.text: Whisk in water, 1 teaspoon at a time, until the dressing drips slowly off the whisk.
steps.look: About as thick as melted ice cream.

steps.text: Pull the romaine leaves apart. Rinse them in the colander.
steps.tip: Look for grit at the bottom of each leaf.

steps.text: Roll the leaves in the kitchen towel and press until they're dry.
steps.look: No drops of water on the leaves.

steps.text: Tear the leaves into bite-size pieces into the large bowl.
steps.tip: Tearing needs no knife and leaves no brown edges.

steps.text: Dip a piece of lettuce in the dressing and taste it. Fix one thing, then taste again.
steps.tip: Too sharp: more mayonnaise. Flat: a pinch of salt or more lemon.

steps.text: Pour the dressing over the lettuce. Add the chicken and the wraps' parmesan, and toss until coated.
Lay a tortilla flat. Pile a quarter of the salad across the bottom third.
steps.tip: Leave 2 inches bare at each side.

steps.text: Fold the two sides over the filling, then roll it up tightly from the bottom. Set it seam side down.
steps.look: A tight roll with closed ends.

steps.text: Fill and roll the other three the same way.
Lay a damp paper towel under the board. Cut each wrap in half on a slant with the bread knife, sawing gently.
steps.tip: Hold the wrap with the claw grip.

steps.text: Eat them right away. Put leftovers in the fridge within 2 hours.
steps.tip: Mayonnaise and chicken shouldn't sit out.

substitutions.note: Greek yogurt makes a tangier dressing. Taste it before adding all the lemon juice.

tear.text: Set aside the 8 biggest leaves whole for wrapping. Tear the rest into bite-size pieces into the large bowl.
tear.tip: Tearing needs no knife and leaves no brown edges. Keep the wrapping leaves on a dry towel.

fill.text: Lay 2 big leaves on a plate, overlapping, rib side down. Pile a quarter of the salad down the middle.
fill.tip: Leave the leaf tips bare so you can fold them up.

roll.text: Fold the sides of the leaves up around the filling, like a taco.
roll.look: Salad snug inside the leaves, with nothing spilling out.

more.text: Fill the other three the same way.

store.text: Eat them right away, holding the sides up. Put leftovers in the fridge within 2 hours.
store.tip: Mayonnaise and chicken shouldn't sit out.

wrong.sign: The leaf tears when you fold it
wrong.fix: Fold along the thick middle rib, not across it, and patch the tear with a second leaf.
Use less filling, overlap two leaves, and hold the sides up as you eat.

How do you make a lettuce wrap sturdy?
quiz.explain: Two leaves overlapped make a wide wrapper that holds the filling.

dry-leaves.title: Dry leaves hold the dressing
dry-leaves.body: Dressing slides off wet lettuce, and the water left on the leaves makes it thin. Lettuce patted dry lets the dressing cling, and the wrapping leaves stay crisp instead of slippery.

roll.title: Two leaves, sides up
roll.body: One leaf is too narrow to hold much. Two big leaves overlapped make a wide, sturdy wrapper. Folding the sides up around the filling, like a taco, keeps it in while you eat.
